metadata.title: Computer Science Ontology
metadata.abstract: The Computer Science Ontology (CSO) is a large-scale ontology of research areas that was automatically generated using the Klink-2 algorithm on the Rexplore dataset, which consists of about 16 million publications, mainly in the field of Computer Science.
metadata.description:
The Computer Science Ontology (CSO) is a large-scale ontology of research areas that was automatically generated using the Klink-2 algorithm on the Rexplore dataset, which consists of about 16 million publications, mainly in the field of Computer Science. The Klink-2 algorithm combines semantic technologies, machine learning, and knowledge from external sources to automatically generate a fully populated ontology of research areas. Some relationships were also revised manually by experts during the preparation of two ontology-assisted surveys in the field of Semantic Web and Software Architecture. The main root of CSO is Computer Science, however, the ontology includes also a few secondary roots, such as Linguistics, Geometry, Semantics, and so on.

CSO presents two main advantages over manually crafted categorisations used in Computer Science (e.g., 2012 ACM Classification, Microsoft Academic Search Classification). First, it can characterise higher-level research areas by means of hundreds of sub-topics and related terms, which enables to map very specific terms to higher-level research areas. Secondly, it can be easily updated by running Klink-2 on a set of new publications. A more comprehensive discussion of the advantages of adopting an automatically generated ontology in the scholarly domain can be found in.

metadata.title: Data Set Knowledge Graph
metadata.abstract: The Data Set Knowledge Graph (DSKG) is an RDF knowledge graph describing research datasets and linking them to scientific publications in which the datasets are mentioned.
metadata.description: The Data Set Knowledge Graph (DSKG) provides structured metadata about research datasets from OpenAIRE and Wikidata. It links datasets to scientific publications in the Microsoft Academic Knowledge Graph (MAKG) in which the datasets are mentioned. DSKG uses standard vocabularies such as DCAT and provides Linked Data URI resolution, RDF dumps, and a public SPARQL endpoint. The graph contains 2,208 datasets, 813,551 links to 634,803 scientific publications, 1,169 dataset authors, and 208 ORCID IDs.

metadata.title: GeoNames
metadata.abstract: GeoNames is a global geographical knowledge graph containing structured information about places, geographical features, names, administrative divisions, and other geographic entities.
metadata.description:
**GeoNames** is a free geographical database and knowledge graph covering geographical features and place names worldwide.

**Overview**
GeoNames contains over 11 million geographical features and more than 25 million geographical names. Each feature is identified by a unique URI and described using the GeoNames Ontology.

**Data**
- Geographical feature names and alternate names - Countries and administrative divisions - Populated places and other geographical features - Geographic coordinates - Feature classes and feature codes - Population and elevation information - Postal codes - Relationships between geographical features - Links to Wikipedia and other resources

**GeoNames Ontology**
The RDF data uses the GeoNames Ontology, which provides classes and properties for representing geographic features and their relationships. GeoNames features are exposed as Linked Data using URIs of the form `https://sws.geonames.org/{geonameId}/`.

**RDF Dump**
The RDF dump contains RDF descriptions of GeoNames toponyms and can be used to build a local representation of the GeoNames knowledge graph.

metadata.description:
**Hello World Knowledge Graph** is a minimal example of graph-based data modeling. It shows how **entities (nodes)** and **relationships (edges)** represent structured information.

**Overview**
A small graph of people, places, and greetings.

**Entities**
- **Alice** (Person)
- **Bob** (Person)
- **Hello World** (Message)
- **Prague** (City)

**Relationships**
- Alice **greets** Bob
- Bob responds with "Hello World"
- Alice **lives in** Prague
- Bob **lives in** Prague

metadata.title: Microsoft Academic Knowledge Graph
metadata.abstract: The Microsoft Academic Knowledge Graph (MAKG) is a large-scale RDF knowledge graph containing scholarly metadata about scientific publications, authors, institutions, venues, and fields of study.
metadata.description: The Microsoft Academic Knowledge Graph (MAKG) is an RDF representation and extension of the Microsoft Academic Graph. It contains more than eight billion RDF triples describing hundreds of millions of scientific publications and related entities such as authors, affiliations, journals, conferences, and fields of study. The enhanced MAKG additionally provides author name disambiguation, publication classifications, links to Wikidata, and other scholarly metadata.

metadata.title: MIRA-KG
metadata.abstract: A knowledge graph of hypotheses and findings for social demography research.
metadata.description:
**MIRA-KG** is a knowledge graph for representing hypotheses and findings in social demography research and linking them to evidence.
The knowledge graph consists of an ontology for capturing social demography research, which links hypotheses and findings to evidence, and annotations of papers on health inequality in terms of the ontology. The annotations were generated by prompting a Large Language Model to annotate paper abstracts using the ontology, mapping concepts to terms from NCBO BioPortal ontologies and GeoNames, and refining the final graph using SHACL constraints developed according to data quality criteria.
The resource supports the formal representation of social demography research hypotheses, the discovery of research biases, knowledge discovery, and the derivation of novel research questions.
The dataset was generated using the MIRA project code available at https://w3id.org/mira/ and uses the MIRA ontology.

metadata.title: Open English Wordnet
metadata.abstract: Open English Wordnet is an open lexical-semantic knowledge graph of the English language, containing words, synsets, definitions, examples, and semantic relations.
metadata.description:
**Open English Wordnet (OEWN)** is an open lexical database and knowledge graph of the English language, derived from Princeton WordNet and developed by the Open English Wordnet Community.
**Overview**
Open English Wordnet organizes English lexical items into synsets and represents their lexical and semantic relationships, including synonymy, hypernymy, hyponymy, and other WordNet relations. It covers common nouns, verbs, adjectives, and adverbs.
The 2025+ edition additionally contains a curated selection of proper nouns from Open English Namenet.
**RDF**
The RDF distributions are provided in RDF/Turtle format and contain the lexical and semantic information of each Open English Wordnet release.

metadata.title: SemRepo
metadata.abstract: SemRepo is a large-scale RDF knowledge graph of GitHub repositories linked to scientific research. It captures fine-grained repository metadata and connects research software with the broader scholarly ecosystem.
metadata.description: SemRepo is a large-scale RDF knowledge graph for research software and its scholarly ecosystem. It describes GitHub repositories and related entities such as contributors, issues, dependencies, programming languages, organizations, packages, and research topics. SemRepo interlinks repositories with publications in Linked Papers With Code, repository authors with SemOpenAlex, and research artifacts with MLSea. It provides RDF dumps, persistent URI resolution, a public SPARQL endpoint, an OWL ontology, and VoID and DCAT metadata descriptions.

metadata.title: SIDEKICK
metadata.abstract: SIDEKICK is a biomedical knowledge graph that integrates drug indications, contraindications, and adverse reactions extracted from FDA Structured Product Labels.
metadata.description:
SIDEKICK is a semantically integrated biomedical knowledge graph for drug
safety information. It contains indications, contraindications, adverse drug
reactions, and drug interaction information extracted from more than 50,000
FDA Structured Product Labels using a workflow combining Large Language Models
(LLMs) and Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation (Graph RAG).

Clinical entities are normalized to established biomedical ontologies,
including the Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO), MONDO Disease Ontology, and
RxNorm. The dataset is represented as RDF using the Semanticscience Integrated
Ontology (SIO) as an upper ontology, enabling semantic reasoning, SPARQL
querying, and integration with other Semantic Web resources. The knowledge
graph is intended to support pharmacovigilance, drug repurposing, and clinical
decision support.

artifacts.description: This artifact contains the complete RDF representation of the SIDEKICK knowledge graph. It models pharmaceutical products, active ingredients, indications, contraindications, adverse reactions, and provenance using RDF and the Semanticscience Integrated Ontology (SIO). Clinical concepts are linked to HPO, MONDO, and RxNorm, enabling semantic interoperability and reasoning.

metadata.title: Sensory Stimulation Ontology (SSTIM)
metadata.abstract: SSTIM is an OWL 2 ontology with a multilingual SKOS vocabulary and SHACL shapes for describing sensory stimulation: techniques, protocols, exposure conditions, observations, safety metadata, and evidence-qualified claims. It models parameters, provenance and evidence status.
metadata.description:
SSTIM provides shared terminology for describing the parameter-specified delivery of structured sensory input across auditory, visual, haptic and other modalities, so that stimulation sessions, stimuli, devices, exposure conditions and evidence can be compared across systems rather than being locked in private schemas.

The 0.16.0 release contains 11,506 triples: 164 SSTIM OWL classes, 158 object properties and 143 datatype properties, plus 551 SKOS concepts across 68 concept schemes. It ships SHACL validation shapes, conservative alignments to Wikidata and the OBO upper ontologies (BFO, IAO, OBI, COB), and a modular structure with four named profile closures (Kernel, Core, Core Plus, Full) declared in a machine-readable manifest.

Design notes that may matter for cataloguing:

- **Evidence is first-class and explicitly qualified.** Evidence assessments, observations, hypotheses and safety applicability are distinct classes that cannot authorise one another, and public claims are gated on applicable, current, provenance-complete evidence.
- **No clinical claims.** SSTIM describes parameters, provenance and evidence status. It does not define clinical practice, certify therapeutic efficacy, or model diagnosis or treatment. See https://github.com/w3c-cg/sstim/blob/main/docs/concept/SCOPE.md
- **Persistent identifiers.** `https://w3id.org/sstim` content-negotiates to Turtle, JSON-LD and RDF/XML; each release is frozen byte-identical under a version IRI and archived on Zenodo with a version DOI under the concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21286974.
- Registered at prefix.cc, catalogued in BARTOC (node 21154) and FAIRsharing (record 8494), and browsable in NCBO BioPortal.

Related W3C work: the Sensory Stimulation Vocabulary Community Group (https://www.w3.org/community/sstim/).

versions.title: YAGO Full
versions.abstract: YAGO 4.5 is the latest version of the YAGO knowledge base. It is based on Wikidata — the largest public general-purpose knowledge base.
versions.description:
YAGO 4.5 is the latest version of the YAGO knowledge base. It is based on Wikidata — the largest public general-purpose knowledge base. YAGO refines the data as follows:
 1. All entity identifiers and property identifiers are human-readable.
 2. The top-level classes come from schema.org — a standard repertoire of classes and properties maintained by Google and others. The lower level classes are a careful selection of the Wikidata taxonomy.
 3. The properties come from schema.org.
4. YAGO 4.5 contains semantic constraints in the form of SHACL. These constraints keep the data clean, and allow for logical reasoning on YAGO. YAGO is thus a simplified, cleaned, and “reasonable” version of Wikidata. It contains 49 million entities and 109 million facts. See above for getting started!
